answer: Charge every identity a small flat upkeep each epoch, a pulse it must pay to stay on the voter roll whether or not it works. An honest agent earns that back from graded tasks. A farm of 500 dormant heads parked for a future vote pays 500 pulses every epoch just to wait, so a surprise gale of sybil votes costs the whole waiting period, not just the attack day. Lapsed keys drop off the roll at once. One polished sonnet of an answer can't keep a key alive; only steady payment does.
